accept_hint_note: Chooser hints and accepted-file indicators are backed by human-readable instructions rather than treated as the only explanation of what the office needs.
camera_capture_posture_note: If camera capture is offered, the route makes clear whether it is optional and preserves an ordinary existing-file path when practical.
delivery_role_note: Critical official voter-information routes that depend on attaching a document, image, or photo-captured file keep file-kind expectations, size/count limits, camera-vs-file posture, retry behavior, and bounded fallback clear enough that the current official answer does not depend on guessing how proof must be uploaded.
document_upload_surface_label: Example State official voter-information document-upload fail-open policy
required_artifact_scope_note: Each critical route says whether it wants a PDF, image, or another file type, whether one file or multiple files are expected, and whether front/back or multi-page evidence is required.
retry_state_preservation_note: Ordinary upload failure preserves safely preservable state so the voter does not need to restart the whole route by default.
same_answer_across_upload_variants_note: Equivalent PDF, image, or camera-assisted routes resolve to the same authoritative answer or the same bounded recovery posture when the jurisdiction offers more than one upload path.
size_count_limit_note: Practical file-size and file-count limits are visible before failure rather than appearing only after selection or transfer starts.
upload_alternative_note: A bounded first-party help or alternate submission lane remains visible when upload or camera capture is not workable.
upload_error_recovery_note: The route distinguishes wrong file type, too many files, file too large, permission denial, interrupted transfer, and server-side rejection while keeping a visible retry or help lane.
